topic: Clearance producer checkpoint data and independent writer boundaries
interpretation: The locator classifies all43 quoted clearance-prefixed names in current SQF. Same-line writer locations do not catch dynamic key arrays or delegated ActorSettings mutations; the counts are not implementation coverage or complete writer proof.

BuildingLaneJournal SAVE is throttled1.5s for unchanged phase and lane roster and requires local group. At group Local loss, a final source checkpoint cannot simply call the ordinary public SAVE or copy the last replicated lane array: it may predate private progress/request/proposal state.

CortexLocality has the private building brain/job before setting cancelled/completed and clearing its machine-local pointers. Capture must use that actual producer data with a controlled freeze boundary before pointer retirement, not a server cache of independently replicated variables.

Current ClearBuilding already aggregates known selected interior settings/motion failures and lane ADOPT before worker startup. This does not prove absent journals were delivered or reconcile every exterior/egress writer.
additionalStateOutsidePrefix: CBE_Operation identity/participants/unavailable and its generation/owner epoch
CBE_BuildingBrain private job/phase/native request ages, progress and spent retry state
CBE_ActorSettings canonical context, actual baseline/applied values and pending restoration; convenience mirrors cannot replace it
CBE_Cortex_ActorMove grenade interruption lease and exact live native destination; source checkpoint cannot replay or overwrite this live reservation
Native group route receipt, actual actor locality, task/destination, settings readbacks and current building transform

writerDomains.domain: Building FSM and its synchronous helpers
writerDomains.finding: Step entry rejects cancelled/finished brain, nonlocal group, epoch or current-brain mismatch. Lane SAVE is callback-tail/coalesced metadata. CHECK/ADOPT never proves all journals delivered.

Preparation/release and dynamic key loops write actor/group state outside the building callback. Settings delegate to canonical ActorSettings. A final main-FSM handle alone is not their completion receipt.

The existing one-shot six-second return callback can retire its exact ActorMove marker on the actor owner even after the group epoch changes. Native follow separately requires current group epoch/generation/route and no owning task. A producer seal must not replay the old interruption or claim this metadata writer ended solely because the building FSM ended.

Independent finite shared-scheduler cleanup exists. Settings cleanup requires current group owner/epoch and no live operation/order/brain; hold cleanup has its own exact issuer/window and one-actor service. These are retirement domains, not resumable room-motion commands.

Discovery/locality/shutdown mutate identity, cleanup and public control independently. Source registration, actual current owner and incoming private epoch must be distinguished; the server private epoch is not the owner epoch.

nextCodeBoundary: Implement a pure producer-side phase snapshot/export from the actual private job, sharing lane validation and preserving original clocks while bypassing publication throttling. It must not publish, replay native commands or set owner-ready. Then integrate authenticated producer registration/final seal and finite request/replay with incoming per-actor actual-native reconciliation. Full writer/phase validation remains required before enabling transport.
limits: Review and locator only: no runtime change, full-build rerun, new test case, package, parity or percentage claim.
Not a complete generic SQF side-effect/callback analysis. Dynamic-key writers and delegated/native interruption domains are explicitly identified, not inferred covered by the locator.
Physical owner-transfer ordering, original-worker quiescence, CQB flow and5/10performance remain unverified; audits paused.
